observed.facings.png: Three facings at one scale on a checkerboard. Each shows a broad, low slab-like body. The top is a cracked clay plate split into polygons by cracks that radiate from a central point. Underneath is a band of brown, wrinkled hide with four to six short, thick limbs that flare at the base. South and north are similar in width and height. East is much longer, since the body is a long oval seen side-on. South and east show a dark fringed slit under the rim; north does not.
observed.south.png: Front view. The cracked-clay top plate is seen at a shallow angle with a slight foreshortening, and its cracks radiate from a reddish centre. Directly under the front rim, a horizontal band of dark grey-brown comb-like fringe (jaw-plates) runs the full width. Below it is a wavy, wrinkled lip of hide. Four stumpy organic limbs end in splayed pad-feet. There are no eyes or pores and no ground shadow. The cut-out is clean.
observed.east.png: Side profile of a long, flat oval body. The cracked clay carapace overhangs a wrinkled brown hide flank. Three visible legs are thick, tapering pillars with flared pads. At the right end, a long, thin fringed mouth slit runs back along the underside of the rim, which marks the right end as the head end. The cut-out is clean.
observed.north.png: Rear view. The same cracked plate and radiating cracks as south, with slightly more saturated, redder rim plates. Under the rim is only folded, muscular hide with no fringe, mouth or eyes. Four limbs are seen from behind. It is slightly blurrier than south. The cut-out is clean.
observed.scale.png: At max zoom beside the vanilla human, the creature is about five cells long and the cracked plate stands at roughly the human's chest height. At 32 px per cell, it reads as a pale orange cracked disc on brown legs, many times larger than the human and the rat. The cracks are still visible as a radial pattern.

SOUTH_FRONT.seen: South shows the front edge with the fringed jaw-plate band and wrinkled lower lip under the rim, across the full width. The front cue is subtle but present.

NORTH_REAR.seen: North shows only folded hide under the rim and rear legs. There is no fringe, mouth, eyes or pits.

NO_OVERHEAD.seen: All three facings use the game's angled camera: the top plate is foreshortened and the legs and flank are visible. None is a plan view.

SAME_SIZE.seen: Code measured a 1% height spread. South and north widths match in facings.png.

SAME_ANIMAL.seen: All views share the same cracked plate, radial crack centre, hide band and pad-footed limbs. The mouth is at the front on south, at the right (head) end on east, and absent on north, so it turns with the body. North rim plates are slightly redder.

SIGNATURE.seen: The clay-pan back has polygon plates and cracks radiating from a centre, which is legible in every facing and at 32 px. The jaw-plate strainer fringe is visible on south and east.

ALIEN.seen: A flat, cracked mud-plate disc on stumpy hide pillars, with a full-width baleen-like mouth slit and no head or neck. A stranger might say 'tortoise' for a moment because of the shell on legs, but the missing head, radial-crack pan and strainer mouth stop it reading as one.

STYLE.seen: Painted textures on the clay and hide with a dark outline. There is no face, eyes or cute features. The finish is slightly smooth and digital but not 3D-render glossy.

OURS.seen: This is a bespoke design with no vanilla or other-mod counterpart. Provenance is polished from its own s1r3.

ALPHA.seen: Real alpha on all facings, with no ground patch or shadow under the feet.

OWNER_NOTES.seen: North is now the same size as south (1% spread), and the cartoonish face is gone; the front cue is jaw-plates only.

SCALE.seen: It is many times the human's footprint, which fits a canyon-floor giant with drawSize 4.6.

LEGIBLE.seen: At 32 px it reads as a pale cracked disc over a dark band of legs, clearly apart from the ground.

reply.subject: RM_Muttavaq
reply.image_seen: Image 1 shows three low, clay-plated creatures at shared scale. Image 2 shows the broad front with a straining band above a folded lower lip. Image 3 shows an elongated side profile with muscular limbs. Image 4 shows a closed rear underside beneath cracked plates. Image 5 shows the creature much larger than a human, including a normal-play inset.

concerns.evidence: North shares the pale ochre upper plates, orange-brown plate edges and dark folded hide visible in south. Its darker forward plate edges remain distinct from the illuminated upper surfaces. Polygon boundaries and the central radiating cracks remain clearly resolved in both the individual north image and the shared-scale panel. The images do not show a conspicuous palette or sharpness mismatch.

The low protective top suggests a tortoise as the nearest comparison, but the visible anatomy reads as an invented creature. The broad, irregular clay-pan plates form a continuous terrain-like mound, the straining jaw band spans the front beneath its rim, and the limbs emerge through muscular hide folds with blunt, toeless ends. South and north lack a projecting tortoise head, recognizable feet or a distinct domed carapace. East makes the unusually elongated, low body especially clear.
